turns.content: In triangle ABC, BC=12 and angle B=30 degrees. Let AC=b and AB=c, and identify which side is opposite the given angle.
Use only the Pythagorean theorem, taking BC as the hypotenuse, to form an equation for c and derive the two-root condition.
Use the sum and product of the two roots to determine when both possible values of c are positive.
Examine the two boundary values of b: one makes the quadratic have a repeated root and the other makes one root zero. Decide whether either boundary gives two valid side lengths.
Check that every b strictly between those boundaries gives two positive roots that satisfy the triangle conditions.
Count the integer values of AC for which two distinct positive values of AB are possible.
